title: Israel Enslaved in Egypt
summary: A new king who does not remember Joseph fears Israel's rapid growth and forces the people into hard labor. When Hebrew midwives refuse to kill newborn boys, Pharaoh orders every infant son thrown into the Nile.

title: Moses Born and Flees
summary: A Hebrew baby is hidden, then set afloat on the Nile and rescued by Pharaoh's daughter, who raises him as her own. Grown, Moses kills an Egyptian, flees to Midian, and marries Zipporah there.

title: The Burning Bush
summary: While tending sheep near Horeb, Moses sees a bush ablaze yet unburned and God speaks to him from within it. God sends Moses to rescue Israel from slavery and, when Moses asks, reveals his covenant name.

title: Moses Sent Back to Egypt
summary: God equips Moses with miraculous signs and answers his objections about speaking ability by appointing Aaron as his mouthpiece. Moses leaves Midian, reunites with Aaron, and together they convince Israel's elders to believe.

title: Pharaoh Refuses and Retaliates
summary: Moses and Aaron ask Pharaoh to let Israel go worship in the wilderness, but he refuses and accuses them of laziness. Pharaoh punishes the request by making the Israelites gather their own straw for bricks.

title: God Renews His Promise
summary: Discouraged by Pharaoh's cruelty, Moses hears God reaffirm his covenant name and his promise to redeem Israel and bring the people into the promised land. God sends Moses and Aaron back to confront Pharaoh again.

title: The Nile Turns to Blood
summary: Aaron's staff becomes a snake and swallows the Egyptian magicians' staffs, but Pharaoh's heart remains hard. Aaron then strikes the Nile with his staff, turning the entire river to blood and killing its fish.

title: Frogs, Gnats, and Flies
summary: Three plagues strike in succession: frogs overrun Egypt until Pharaoh briefly relents, dust turns to gnats that even the magicians cannot reproduce, and swarms of flies fill Egyptian homes while sparing Israel's land of Goshen.

title: Livestock, Boils, and Hail
summary: A plague kills Egypt's livestock while Israel's animals are spared, painful boils break out on the Egyptians, and a violent hailstorm mixed with fire destroys crops and anything left exposed across the land.

title: Locusts and Darkness
summary: A locust swarm devours every plant the hail left standing, stripping Egypt bare. Then a thick, unnatural darkness covers the land for three days while Israel's homes remain lit, and still Pharaoh refuses to yield.

title: Warning of the Final Plague
summary: God tells Moses one more plague remains: the death of every firstborn in Egypt. This time Pharaoh himself will beg Israel to leave, and Moses warns Pharaoh directly before the plague falls that night.

title: The Passover and the Exodus
summary: God institutes the Passover meal and the protective blood on Israel's doorframes. The tenth plague kills every Egyptian firstborn, Pharaoh finally releases Israel, and the people leave Rameses after four hundred thirty years in Egypt.

title: Consecration and the Pillar
summary: God commands that every firstborn male among Israel's people and animals be set apart to him as a lasting reminder of the exodus. God then leads the people by a visible pillar of cloud and fire.

title: Crossing the Red Sea
summary: Pharaoh changes his mind and pursues Israel, trapping the people against the sea. The LORD parts the water so Israel crosses on dry ground, then closes the sea again and drowns the pursuing Egyptian army.
